extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys subject to USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings; OED and USPTO decisionmakers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures the USPTO applies when deciding whether to impose reciprocal discipline based on a state's disciplinary adjudication (per 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and Selling v. Radford). Explains burdens of proof, exceptions that preclude reciprocal discipline, procedural notice/response requirements, and consequences/reinstatement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling / 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) standard (exceptions to reciprocal discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Selling, state disbarment creates a federal-level presumption that imposition of reciprocal discipline is proper unless an independent review of the record reveals: (1) a want of due process; (2) an infirmity of proof of the misconduct; or (3) that grave injustice would result from the imposition of reciprocal discipline. The USPTO regulation mirrors these elements and adds (iv) any argument that the practitioner was not publicly censured, publicly reprimanded, placed on probation, disbarred, suspended or disciplinarily disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text of 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) is controlling. A respondent must identify one of these grounds and demonstrate a genuine issue of material fact by clear and convincing evidence. The Director considers timely filed responses but does not act as a court of review to relitigate state proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's burden of proof (clear and convincing; genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent reciprocal discipline, the respondent is required to demonstrate, by clear and convincing evidence, that there is a genuine issue of material fact as to one of the Selling elements (due process, infirmity of proof, or grave injustice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal courts have held the respondent's burden is narrow; the USPTO Director is not 'sitting as a court of review.' Mere disagreement with the state factfinder or the weight given evidence is insufficient. The showing must be clear and convincing and establish a genuine factual dispute on one of the enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process deficiency standard in disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Due process requires 'the opportunity to be heard at a meaningful time and in a meaningful manner' including reasonable notice of charges, opportunity to respond, attend and participate in hearings, present evidence, testify, call and cross-examine witnesses, and make arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing of deprivation of due process requires more than an unsworn statement; the respondent must demonstrate the state tribunal failed to follow notice/service or hearing procedures (e.g., certified/registered mail to last address of record) or otherwise deprived the practitioner of the meaningful opportunity to be heard. If the record shows attendance, representation by counsel, and opportunities to present and challenge evidence, due process is typically satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infirmity of proof defense (high threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: To invoke infirmity of proof, respondent must show 'such an infirmity of proof' establishing the conduct 'as to give rise to the clear conviction' that the Office could not accept the state's conclusion as final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a difficult showing; it requires more than challenging the factfinder's weighing of evidence or pointing to mitigating facts (e.g., completion of treatment programs). Absent clear defects in the proof of the underlying misconduct, infirmity of proof will not preclude reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grave injustice analysis (whether sanction fits the misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grave injustice inquiry focuses on whether the severity of the punishment 'fits' the misconduct — i.e., whether the discipline imposed by the state falls outside the range of appropriate sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may consider mitigating factors but will not find grave injustice merely because the respondent believes the state sanction was unjust. If the state discipline is within the appropriate range of penalties for the misconduct, reciprocal discipline is not a grave injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for notice and response under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) files a Request for Notice and Order and the USPTO Director issues a Notice and Order giving the respondent (here 40 days) to file a response containing all information the respondent believes sufficient to establish, by clear and convincing evidence, a genuine issue of material fact that reciprocal discipline would be unwarranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice is sent by certified mail; respondents may request extensions (partially granted in this case). The OED Director files a response to the respondent's submission and the respondent may file a reply. Failure to timely and substantively contest the grounds limits relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available reciprocal sanctions and identity rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall impose the identical public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification as imposed by the state unless an exception is proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identical-sanction rule means the Office applies the same category of discipline (e.g., exclusion/disbarment) absent a successful showing under Selling/§ 11.24(d)(1). In this case, exclusion from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters was imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and operational obligations following exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon exclusion, the practitioner must comply with duties set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and, if seeking reinstatement, with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60; the USPTO shall dissociate the practitioner's name from any Customer Numbers and electronic system accounts and the practitioner may not obtain or be added to a Customer Number until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies concrete operational steps: dissociation from Customer Numbers, prohibition on applying for or obtaining Customer Numbers, and compliance with reinstatement procedures. Reinstatement eligibility here is no earlier than five years from the effective date (per 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO/OED notice and publication obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a notice materially consistent with the Final Order in the Official Gazette and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where the practitioner is admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review (e.g., OED FOIA Reading Room). Publication and interjurisdictional notice are standard administrative steps to inform disciplinary bodies and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate conduct and regulatory violation (basis for reciprocal discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be predicated upon a practitioner's disbarment by a state for conduct violating state rules or criminal laws (here, the Michigan order was based on convictions and violation of Michigan Court Rule 9.104(5) and supporting findings), which is treated as a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites the underlying criminal convictions (aggravated theft, drug possession, tampering with evidence) as the factual predicate. When state discipline is grounded in criminal convictions or other serious professional misconduct, USPTO reciprocal discipline typically follows unless one of the Selling exceptions is established.
